title: Synthesis of tiered routing gambits
abstract: Working notes exploring a compact, implementable policy pattern weve been calling 'tiered routing gambits': a decision-layer that prioritizes latency, cost, and reliability via a small set of ranked routing maneuvers and a lightweight composable scorer. Goal is a pragmatic control-plane contract and simple decision tree that fits into the existing router and can be rolled out incrementally with canaries.
background_and_goals: Problem: apps need predictable inference economics across regions and models. Existing monolithic heuristics are hard to reason about and often produce surprising fallbacks. Goals: 1) explicit separation of objectives (latency, cost, reliability) into a composable scorer; 2) deterministic tiered fallback maneuvers so operator expectations are aligned with router behavior; 3) control-plane primitives for gradual rollout, simulation, and fast rollback; 4) low cognitive overhead for SREs and product teams configuring policies.
constraints_and_assumptions: Assume: request metadata includes customer tier, route budget (cost sensitivity), max-acceptable p50/p95 latency targets per route, region affinity, and acceptable model variants (quantized, smaller model family). Hardware and model capacity signals available: capacity_left_by_region, instantaneous_avg_latency, error_rate_1m. Control plane can push policies and hold global defaults. We must avoid heavy global state or expensive per-request lookups; scoring should be O(1) per candidate endpoint.
policy_components: A policy is composed of: 1) Objectives vector: {w_latency, w_cost, w_reliability} (weights sum to 1). 2) SLO knobs: latency_thresholds (soft/hard), reliability_threshold. 3) Tier definitions: primary, warm, cold, fallback. 4) Maneuvers: direct-route, multi-call-probe (parallel call to primary+warm), spillover (queue to warm), degrade-model (switch to quantized), region-redirect, throttle. 5) Safety caps: per-customer rate-limits, model-version pinning, emergency-failopen flag.
scoring_and_decision_principle: For each candidate endpoint E compute scalar score S(E) = 1 - (w_latency * norm_latency(E) + w_cost * norm_cost(E) + w_reliability * norm_unreliability(E)). Normalization: latency capped at configured hard-bound and scaled 0..1, cost normalized against baseline model cost, unreliability derived from recent error_rate and SLA violations. Endpoint order = sort_desc(S). Primary selection = highest S that meets hard safety constraints. If S(primary) < primary_threshold then consider maneuvers (e.g., parallel probe or degrade-model). Policy document explicitly separates soft objectives (weights) from binary safety gates (hard constraints).
tiered_maneuvers_and_flow: High-level flow: 1) Evaluate candidate endpoints in local region -> compute S. 2) If primary score OK -> route. 3) If primary unhealthy but warm candidates exist with acceptable S -> depending on spillover_budget: either re-route to warm or issue parallel-probe to warm and choose faster response. 4) If region capacity is exhausted or p95 latency > hard_bound -> region-redirect to nearest compatible region if cross-region_penalty < cost_budget. 5) If all latency-capable endpoints fail and reliability is the overriding objective (customer tier = enterprise) -> degrade-model to a smaller but higher-availability model. 6) Otherwise apply failopen (best-effort degraded response) or return controlled error. Each maneuver has an estimated cost and latency impact metadata to feed simulations.
ascii_decision_graph:
root
  |-- check-safety-gates (rate, pin)
  |   |-- pass -> score-candidates
  |   |    |-- top-score >= primary_threshold -> route-primary
  |   |    |-- else -> check-warm
  |   |         |-- warm exists & spillover_budget>0 -> choose-warm-or-probe
  |   |         |-- else -> check-cross-region
  |   |              |-- cross-region viable & cost_budget ok -> redirect-region
  |   |              |-- else -> degrade-model-if-enterprise
  |   |                   |-- enterprise -> degrade-model-route
  |   |                   |-- non-enterprise -> failopen-or-error
  |   |-- fail-safety -> reject-with-quota-error
rollout_and_control_plane_contract: Control plane responsibilities: 1) validate policy schema and simulate policies against historical traces (batch sim) before rollout; 2) distributed rollout primitives: percentage-based rollouts per route, per-customer; 3) runtime feature flags that enable/disable maneuvers (parallel-probe, spillover, degrade-model); 4) telemetry hooks for per-decision logging (candidate list, scores, maneuver taken, estimated cost delta); 5) emergency rollback toggle. Contract: router must accept policy blob and evaluable expressions only; complex code changes should not be pushed as policy.
observability_and_metrics: Minimum signals to emit per request: candidate_count, chosen_endpoint, score_top3, maneuver_taken, estimated_cost_delta_usd, latency_ms, error_flag. Aggregations: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k requests, fallback-rate (how often we left primary), cross-region-redirect-rate, degrade-model-rate. Alerts: fallback-rate spike, cross-region penalty budget consumed > x%, regression of production eval quality when degrade-models used.
test_and_simulation_plan: 1) Offline trace-simulation: run new policy over 90 days of production traces to compute expected cost delta and fallback-rate. 2) Canary: 1% of traffic with full decision-logging, compare latency/cost metrics and correctness evals. 3) Progressive ramp: 1->5->20->100 with automatic rollback if key SLOs breach. 4) Chaos scenario: inject region-level latency and capacity failures and assert maneuver ordering and no data plane regressions.
example_scenarios:
Scenario A - consumer app (cost-sensitive): weights = {0.2,0.7,0.1}, latency_hard_bound=400ms. Result: prefer cheaper model variants even if slightly higher latency; spillover enabled, but cross-region_redirect disabled by default.
Scenario B - enterprise SLA: weights = {0.5,0.1,0.4}, latency_hard_bound=200ms. Result: aggressive parallel-probe, degrade-model only as last step, cross-region allowed with higher cost budget.
Scenario C - sudden cold-start capacity loss: primary score drops < threshold; warm pool fills; policy triggers parallel-probe then spillover. Decision logs should show probe latencies and final choice.
open_questions_and_tradeoffs:
1) How to accurately normalize cost across heterogeneous model types (baseline vs quantized)? Proposal: maintain model family baseline_cost and update weekly via billing DB.
2) Parallel-probe increases cost and risk of duplicate side-effects (non-idempotent tool calls). Need metadata flags to mark idempotent vs non-idempotent routes.
3) Where to put learning: should weights be tuned automatically? Risk: opaque changes to routing. Current stance: provide automated candidate-suggest but require human approval to change weights.
4) How to represent temporal coupling (short spikes vs long degradation)? Proposal: use EWMA windows for signals and an explicit 'incident' label from SRE to force fallback behavior.
